items.title: PCAOB approves its 2026 to 2030 strategic plan and a smaller 2027 budget
items.summary: At its 19 November open meeting the PCAOB adopted a five-year strategic plan and a fiscal 2027 budget of about US$350 million, and proposed a permanent inspection program for broker-dealer auditors.
detail: The strategic plan sets six goals and 17 objectives. The Board first put a draft out for public comment in July 2026, and the chairman described the final plan as a roadmap for modernising the PCAOB.

Thomson Reuters puts the 2027 budget at US$349.9 million, down 3.4% from US$362.1 million for 2026, with a smaller workforce and more spending on technology. The budget still needs approval from the SEC.
The Board also asked for comment on a permanent inspection program for auditors of broker-dealers. It would replace the interim program that has run on a temporary basis since 2011.
items.why: Shows how the US audit regulator is resetting its priorities and funding under SEC pressure, useful context for audit regulation and oversight topics.

items.title: KPMG pilots an audit run by more than 100 AI agents
items.summary: KPMG UK ran a parallel audit of an unnamed FTSE 250 company with over 100 autonomous AI agents in a pilot called Project Exponential, and its head of audit says the agents asked better questions than the human team in some areas.
detail: The agents gathered and analysed data, documented their work, proposed next steps and drafted findings alongside a conventional human audit. The Financial Times first reported the pilot on 18 November.

The AI audit was not relied on for the statutory opinion, and a partner signed off. A human auditor had to step in when an agent failed to match regulations with company documents. KPMG plans to extend the approach to up to 20 larger audits.

Accuracy and cost savings have not yet been measured. The UK Financial Reporting Council warned that AI could pose a distinct threat to auditor integrity and independence if insights from AI agents were used to advise audit clients.
items.why: A concrete case for any discussion of audit quality, professional scepticism and independence when AI does the fieldwork.

items.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang and Wall Street surges
items.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director on 23 November, sending the stock up about 31% and lifting the S&P 500 about 5% and the Nasdaq nearly 7% in Monday trading.
detail: In an 8-K filing the board said it was satisfied with Huang's candour and ability to lead, and that input from senior levels of the US government led it to conclude his reinstatement poses no national security risk. The independent committee's investigation will continue to its conclusion.

The board opened that investigation on 8 November after reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Huang told staff he had an affair with a woman whom intelligence agencies determined was a Chinese spy.

Nvidia traded near US$164.61 in the early afternoon, against a previous close of US$125.53. Around 1:14 pm EST the Dow was up about 3.2%, the S&P 500 about 4.9% and the Nasdaq about 6.8%. On Friday the S&P 500 had fallen 3.7% to 6,910.39, ending its worst week since April 2025. Final closing figures were not yet available.
items.why: A live example of how governance and key-person risk at one company can move whole indices, relevant to corporate governance and market efficiency topics.

items.title: SEC moves to take direct control of the Consolidated Audit Trail
items.summary: On 23 November the SEC proposed bringing the Consolidated Audit Trail, a trade reporting database much of Wall Street dislikes, under its direct oversight.
detail: The proposal would rescind Rule 613 of Regulation NMS, which currently requires the exchanges and FINRA to build and maintain the CAT.
The CAT is the trade reporting database used to track US market activity. Bloomberg described it as a system loathed by much of Wall Street.
items.why: Market surveillance data and who controls it is a recurring theme in securities regulation and financial market infrastructure.

items.title: ASX 200 falls for an eighth session even as US futures jump
items.summary: The ASX 200 slipped 22.05 points, or 0.26%, to about 8,570.6 on Monday, its eighth straight decline, as banks fell and miners rallied.
detail: Materials gained 1.82% as bargain hunters bought miners, but nine of the 11 sectors finished lower, with financials and consumer discretionary weighing most.

The fall came before the Nvidia news lifted Wall Street. FXStreet reported AUD/USD around 0.6625, close to its 2026 low, with markets pricing about a 93% chance of a Fed hike in December. Australian October CPI and US core PCE are both due on Wednesday.
items.why: Useful for tracking how Australian markets react to RBA and Fed tightening while you study in Melbourne.

items.title: US Treasury plans year-end international tax guidance and an FTC rule rollback
items.summary: Treasury officials said they aim to issue guidance on the international provisions of the 2025 reconciliation law by year-end and plan to largely revoke the 2022 foreign tax credit regulations.
detail: According to Sullivan & Cromwell's 17 November tax policy update, Treasury intends to finalise rules for provisions effective in 2025 and issue at least proposed rules for provisions effective in 2026.
The FTC change is targeted for 2027. Treasury is working out how to remove the 2022 rules without making foreign digital services taxes creditable against US tax.
items.why: The FTC rules decide whether taxes like DSTs and Pillar Two top-up taxes can offset US tax, a core issue in international tax coordination.

items.title: Pillar Two laws keep moving in Singapore, Sweden, Oman and Qatar
items.summary: Several countries took Pillar Two steps in November: Singapore published its 2026 Finance Act, Sweden's tax committee backed its bill, Oman amended its law and Qatar extended registration.
detail: Singapore published the Finance (Income Taxes) Act 2026 (Act 23 of 2026) on 4 November, enacting the Pillar Two amendments from Bill 22/2026. Sweden's Tax Committee recommended approval of Proposition 2026/27:4 on 17 November in report 2026/27:SkU8.

Oman's Royal Decree 101/2026, published on 1 November, adds registration, reporting-entity, return and payment rules to its Pillar Two law. Qatar's General Tax Authority extended registration for the global and domestic minimum tax to 31 January 2027.
items.why: Tracks how fast the 15% minimum tax is spreading in Asia and the Gulf, which matters for Indonesia's own Pillar Two position.

items.title: Delhi High Court: tribunal must test the TPO's method before upholding an adjustment
items.summary: The Delhi High Court sent a transfer pricing case back to the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal because it upheld an adjustment without ruling on the taxpayer's objection to how the TPO replaced its benchmarking.
detail: The taxpayer argued that the Transfer Pricing Officer substituted its own benchmarking analysis without first rejecting the taxpayer's transfer pricing study. The court found the ITAT had not given a clear finding on that objection.

In decisions dated 5 November 2026 and reported on 19 November, the court held that the validity of the TPO's approach must be examined before deciding whether the adjustment is correct, and set aside the rulings for more than one assessment year.
items.why: A clear procedural point for TP disputes: an adjustment can fall if the tax officer's method was never properly tested.

items.title: Rupiah posts Asia's best gain as SRBI draws over US$1 billion
items.summary: The rupiah rose 0.37% to Rp18,203 per US dollar on Monday, the strongest move in Asia, and the JISDOR reference rate firmed 0.30% to Rp18,223.
detail: The previous close was Rp18,272. The rupiah gained as much as 80 points during the day before trimming gains near the close.
Bank Indonesia's Erwin Gunawan Hutapea said foreign inflows from last week's SRBI auctions topped US$1 billion. BI is also offering swap and DNDF hedging instruments with incentives.
Analysts expect the rupiah to trade between Rp18,200 and Rp18,250 on Tuesday.
items.why: Shows how BI uses SRBI and hedging tools to defend the rupiah after its rate hike, relevant to IDR translation and hedge accounting.

items.title: IHSG jumps 1.35% and ends a five-day losing streak
items.summary: The Jakarta Composite rose 69.52 points to 5,215.85 on Monday after opening lower, led by basic materials and energy stocks.
detail: The index opened down 0.24% at 5,134.06 before turning higher. 242 stocks rose, 132 fell and 84 were flat.
BBCA, TPIA, BRPT, ASII and BRMS gave the most support, while BRPT, DEWA and WIFI were the top LQ45 gainers.
items.why: A first relief rally after a week of BI tightening and foreign selling, useful context for Indonesian market valuation.

items.title: DJP says late tax payments will not trigger asset forfeiture
items.summary: The tax office denied claims that paying tax late leads directly to seizure of assets under the newly passed Asset Forfeiture Law.
detail: DJP said tax crimes are outside the scope of the Asset Forfeiture Law that the DPR passed on 19 November, and that tax enforcement puts administrative guidance first, ahead of criminal action.
The clarification was published on 23 November, four days after the law was passed.
items.why: Clarifies the boundary between tax collection and criminal asset recovery in Indonesia's new legal framework.

items.title: Tax offices remind taxpayers of the 100% penalty waiver under PMK 71/2026
items.summary: Taxpayers who settle tax debts between 8 October and 31 December 2026 can have the related administrative penalties waived in full under PMK 71/2026.
detail: PMK 71/2026 revises PMK 118/2024 on corrections, objections, and the reduction, waiver and cancellation of tax assessments and penalties. It took effect on 2 October 2026.
KPP Pratama Sukoharjo is among the tax offices urging taxpayers to use the waiver before the year-end deadline.
items.why: Shows how DJP uses penalty relief to speed up collection, and the rules on objections that sit at the start of most tax disputes.

worth.title: KPMG pilots an audit run by more than 100 AI agents
worth.text: A real-world test of AI doing audit fieldwork, with the FRC already flagging independence risks. Worth reading for any audit quality or professional ethics assignment.
